cards.text: Jesus comes back to the rest of His disciples and finds a large crowd around them, with scribes, teachers of the law, arguing with them. You leave the group chat for ONE afternoon and come back to four hundred messages.

cards.question: As soon as all the people in that crowd see Jesus, how do they react?

answers.text: They're filled with awe and run to greet Him
They go quiet and slowly back away from Him
They keep on arguing and pay Him no mind

cards.text: Jesus asks, "What are you disputing with them?" Whole debate going, and the one who answers is a dad in the crowd: "Teacher, I brought You my son…"

cards.question: The dad says his son has a spirit that makes him ___.

cards.text: Whenever the spirit seizes the boy, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth and becomes rigid.

cards.question: The dad asked Jesus' disciples to drive the spirit out, but they were ___.

cards.text: Jesus answers, "O unbelieving generation! How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you?" Whew. Nobody in that crowd is reaching for a snack right now.

cards.question: Right after calling them an unbelieving generation, what does Jesus tell them to do?
When they bring the boy, the spirit sees Jesus and immediately throws the boy into a convulsion.
Jesus asks the boy's father how long this has been with him. The dad says it only started recently.

cards.text: The dad says the spirit often throws his son into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. Then he begs: "But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us."

cards.question: Jesus echoes part of the dad's request right back at him. Which part?
Then Jesus tells the dad that all things are possible to him who ___.

cards.text: The boy's father answers right away, no speech and no polish. That man skips the small talk like his phone's on 1%.

cards.question: When the boy's father cries out to Jesus, what does he say about his own faith?

answers.text: He believes and asks for help with his unbelief
He has always believed without a single doubt
He doesn't believe at all and needs a sign

cards.text: Jesus sees that a crowd has come running. So He rebukes the unclean spirit: "You deaf and mute spirit."

cards.question: Jesus commands the deaf and mute spirit to come out of the boy and never ___ him again.

cards.text: The spirit shrieks, convulses the boy violently, and comes out. The boy becomes like a corpse, so that many say, "He is dead."

cards.question: While the boy lies there like a corpse, Jesus takes him by the hand and helps him to his feet.
Later in the house, the disciples ask Jesus privately why they couldn't drive the spirit out. What does Jesus say this kind can only come out by?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 7 quotes "O unbelieving generation! How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 16 quotes "You deaf and mute spirit.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card spends words defining 'scribes' as 'teachers of the law.' Hard words get a dictionary pop-up instead.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'away' is a different kind of thing from 'unable' and 'unwilling.' It is a location, not an ability or a will. The question also rules it out, since the dad says he asked the disciples, so they were there.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question's own setup (the dad asked the disciples) rules out the wrong answer 'away.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke mentions a 'snack,' which is a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The card runs past 2 sentences: the narration with the quote, then 'Whew.', then the joke line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says the father 'answers.' Mark 9:24 says he 'cried out.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'So He rebukes the unclean spirit' turns the crowd running up into Jesus' reason for rebuking the spirit. Mark 9:25 only says 'When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked,' which is a time marker, not a stated reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Several story cards (5, 11, 16, 18) are flat retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Across the stop, only cards 1, 7 and 14 try for a laugh, and those are mild.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
